kangaroo-at-2016-felix-01.title: Count the ends
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-01.body:
Every rope has 2 ends, and each end is marked with a dot. Count the dots: there are 6. So there are $6 \div 2 = 3$ ropes.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-01.title: Follow each rope
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-01.body:
Start at one dot and follow the rope through the tangle to its other dot. Cross off both dots. Repeat until all dots are used: you follow 3 ropes.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-03.title: Find the way out
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-03.body:
From O, move around the inner ring until you find a gap in its wall. Go through it into the next ring, then follow that ring to its gap, and so on. Following the gaps from the inside to the outside leads to point **C** at the top. The points A, B, D and E are in parts of the labyrinth that are closed off from this path.

**Answer: (C) C**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-03.title: Work backwards
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-03.body:
Start at each letter and try to reach the middle. From A, B, D and E you always hit a wall before reaching O; from C you can go through the gaps in the walls all the way to O.

**Answer: (C) C**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-04.title: Don't forget Robert
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-04.body:
Of the 10 friends, 6 are girls, so $10 - 6 = 4$ friends are boys. Robert himself is a boy too, so there are $4 + 1 = 5$ boys at the party.

**Answer: (B) 5**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-05.title: Count from 1
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-05.body:
Houses 1 to 47 are 47 houses. Houses 1 to 14 do not get one: 14 houses. So $47 - 14 = 33$ houses get a flyer.

**Answer: (C) 33**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-06.title: Count the cubes
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-06.body:
He must use exactly 10 cubes (or at most 10). Count the cubes in each solid, including hidden cubes that hold up the cubes on top.

Solid A has 10 cubes. Each of the other solids needs more than 10 cubes (11 or 12 when you include the hidden ones), so they cannot be built.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-07.title: Checkerboard
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-07.body:
The box has 2 rows of 3 places. Each egg touches the eggs next to it in its row and the egg above or below it.

Put brown eggs like a checkerboard: top-left, top-right and bottom-middle. None of them touch, so 3 brown eggs are possible.

4 is impossible: each column has 2 places that touch each other, so each of the 3 columns can have at most 1 brown egg.

**Answer: (C) 3**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-08.title: Take away the cat
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-08.body:
The cat has 4 legs. The other $20 - 4 = 16$ legs belong to chickens. Each chicken has 2 legs: $16 \div 2 = 8$ chickens.

**Answer: (C) 8**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-08.title: Check an option
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-08.body:
With 8 chickens: $8 \times 2 = 16$ legs, plus 4 cat legs is 20. ✓

**Answer: (C) 8**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-09.title: Rooms with light
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-09.body:
Each lit room shows 2 bright windows. 18 bright windows means $18 \div 2 = 9$ rooms had the light on. So $12 - 9 = 3$ rooms had the light off.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-09.title: Dark windows
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-09.body:
All 12 rooms have $12 \times 2 = 24$ windows. $24 - 18 = 6$ windows were dark, which is $6 \div 2 = 3$ rooms.

**Answer: (B) 3**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-10.title: Both get older
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-10.body:
In 4 years Paul is 4 years older and Josef is also 4 years older. Together they gain $4 + 4 = 8$ years: $12 + 8 = 20$.

**Answer: (E) 20**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-10.title: Try an example
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-10.body:
Say Paul is 5 and Josef is 7 (together 12). In 4 years they are 9 and 11, together $9 + 11 = 20$.

**Answer: (E) 20**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-11.title: Walk the road
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-11.body:
Follow the road from 1 and look at your right hand side each time the road turns:

- Up the right side: **K** is on the right (A at the top is on the left).
- Along the top to the left: nothing on the right.
- Down the left side: **N** is on the right.
- Along the bottom: G is on the left.
- Up the inner right side: **A** is on the right (R is on the left).
- Along to the left and down to point 2: **O** is on the right (the top O is on the left).

The word is KNAO.

**Answer: (A) KNAO**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-12.title: Fit the pieces
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-12.body:
Each piece is a T made of 4 squares, so every shape must have a number of squares that is a multiple of 4, and you must be able to cover it with T's without gaps.

Try to cover each shape with T pieces, starting in a corner square, which can only be covered in a few ways. Shapes A, B, C and E can be covered. In shape D, after placing a T to cover one end, the squares left over cannot all be covered by T's.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-13.title: Sparrow by sparrow
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-13.body:
Number the sparrows 1 to 5 from the left. In the picture, sparrows 1, 3 and 5 look right and sparrows 2 and 4 look left.

- Sparrow 1 looks right: sees 2, 3, 4, 5 → 4 whistles.
- Sparrow 2 looks left: sees 1 → 1 whistle.
- Sparrow 3 looks right: sees 4, 5 → 2 whistles.
- Sparrow 4 looks left: sees 1, 2, 3 → 3 whistles.
- Sparrow 5 looks right: sees nobody → 0.

Total: $4 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 0 = 10$.

**Answer: (D) 10**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-14.title: Match ladybirds to flowers
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-14.body:
For each ladybird count the points on the two wings: (5 and 2), (4 and 2), (4 and 3), (5 and 3), (6 and 1).

For each flower count petals and leaves: A 7 petals and 5 leaves, B 7 and 1, C 8 and 2, D 7 and 3, E 7 and 2.

- 6 and 1: total 7, difference 5 → flower A.
- 4 and 3: total 7, difference 1 → flower B.
- 5 and 3: total 8, difference 2 → flower C.
- 5 and 2: total 7, difference 3 → flower D.

Flower E (7 petals, 2 leaves) would need a ladybird with 7 points and a difference of 2. That is impossible: two numbers that differ by 2 are both even or both odd, so their total is even, never 7.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2016-felix-15.title: Find all neighbours
kangaroo-at-2016-felix-15.body:
A side touches 4 other sides and is opposite to the last one.

- 1st position: the small square is on top, next to the side with one line and the side with the small diamond.
- 2nd position: the small square is in front, next to the cross (+) and the X.

So the small square touches the line, the small diamond, the + and the X. The only side it does not touch is the big diamond: they are opposite.

**Answer: (C)**
